Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Time, the calendar & feasts · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

spend verb

time

also spend time, pass the day, spend the day, spend the holidays

classical

Tac. Germ. 17.1: tōtōs diēs jūxtā focum atque ignem agunt
Traupman 383: spend (time), agō, cōnsūmō
Traupman 54: fēriās agere

agō, agere, ēgī, āctum

verb, third conjugation

spend, pass (time)

With the time as its object: diem, aestātem, fēriās, vītam agere; “very frequent and classical” in this sense (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • dēgō, dēgere, dēgī — spend, pass (a day, one’s life)

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Plaut. Most. 534: in forō dēgō diem

    Most often with aetātem or vītam: to live out one’s days.

  • cōnsūmō, cōnsūmere, cōnsūmpsī, cōnsūmptum — spend (time) in or on something

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 11.27.5: hōrāsque multās saepe suāvissimō sermōne cōnsūmerēs; Servius Sulpicius in Cic. Fam. 4.12.1: eumque diem ibi cōnsūmpsī

    With the ablative, or in and the ablative, of what fills the time.

Examples

  • cētera intēctī tōtōs diēs jūxtā focum atque ignem agunt

    otherwise unclothed, they spend whole days by the hearth and the fireTac. Germ. 17.1

  • ut domum ventitārēs hōrāsque multās saepe suāvissimō sermōne cōnsūmerēs

    that you would often come to my house and spend many hours in the most delightful conversationCic. Fam. 11.27.5

  • ā mānī ad noctem ūsque in forō dēgō diem

    from morning to night I spend the whole day in the forumPlaut. Most. 534

See also pass the time, waste time, spend the night, spend the winter, spend.
